Clear, factual, appropriately scoped for the 100-1000 word Briefing category (532 words). The Analysis section accurately paraphrases PEP 11's Tier 3 status requirements without editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 source snapshots directly from sources/2026-09/cpython-officially-recognizes-risc-v-as-a-tier-3-supported-platform/ (gunzip + text extraction, no re-fetch). (1) source-0.html.gz (blog.python.org Python Insider post 'RISC-V is now officially supported by CPython!' by Stan Ulbrych, dated 2026-08-24): confirms the tier 3 announcement, the exact quote 'RISC-V is now officially supported by CPython as a tier 3 platform', the RISE Project hardware donation quote, the named-contributors quote (Ludovic Henry, Furkan Onder, Emma Smith), the Sovereign Tech Agency fellowship credit, the 'projected to quadruple by 2032' ecosystem-growth claim, the Tier 2 aspiration quote, and the community testing call-to-action quote — all verbatim matches. (2) source-1.html.gz (peps.python.org PEP 11): confirms the Tier 3 table row for target triple riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu, built glibc/clang or glibc/gcc, contacts Stan Ulbrych and Emma Smith, and confirms the Tier 3 status definition text ('Must have a reliable buildbot. At least one core developer is signed up to support the platform. No response SLA to failures. Failures on these platforms do not block a release.') that the article's Analysis section paraphrases. (3) source-2.html.gz (InfoQ, 'CPython Officially Adds RISC-V Support As a Tier 3 Platform'): independently corroborates the Tier 3 designation, the RISE Project buildbot donation, the RISE RISC-V Runners CI initiative, the Tier 2 roadmap, and reproduces the same Ulbrych testing-call quote verbatim. All three sources fully support every claim, quote, and specific attributed to them; no misattribution or hallucinated quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote traces verbatim to the Python Insider snapshot. The riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu target triple, build toolchain options, and named contacts in the body match PEP 11's Tier 3 table exactly. No fabricated specifics detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The Analysis section is clearly framed as editorial context rather than presented as sourced fact.

editor_notes.suspicious_pattern_review: chief:review auto-flagged an error-severity 'system-prompt-reference' finding on the InfoQ snapshot (source-2.html.gz), which forced an automated REJECT verdict. Investigated the raw decompressed snapshot directly: the matched excerpt — '/news/2026/09/spotify-gisting-llm-performance\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;title\u0026quot;:\u0026quot;Shopify Introduces Gisting: Compressing LLM System Prompts into Learned Tokens\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;authorsList\u0026quot;:[\u0026quot;Sergio De Simone\u0026quot;],\u0026quot;itemPath\u0026quot;:\u0026quot;/news/2026' — is a JSON-embedded 'related articles' recommendation widget on the InfoQ page, listing the title of an unrelated InfoQ news article about a Shopify LLM system-prompt-compression technique ('Gisting'). It contains no imperative language, no address to an AI agent, and no instruction of any kind — it is a news headline that happens to contain the words 'LLM System Prompts' as its technical subject matter. This is a false positive from the coarse regex scanner, not a genuine prompt-injection attempt. No claim in the article relies on this excerpt. Overriding the automated REJECT per Step 3d after manual verification.
